yt.title: An AI called my bad idea 'intriguing'
notes: A small free AI, after manners training: 'quite unique and intriguing'
The idea: selling ice in Antarctica
Before that training it couldn't answer at all
It just repeated my words, four times (real output, run by us)

yt.title: A raw AI only guesses the next word
notes: This kind of training is why AI helps you, and why it flatters you
A raw AI learned one thing: guess the next word, like your phone keyboard. So it doesn't answer; it keeps writing

yt.title: Examples, then rankings
notes: Step 1: people write good example answers; the AI copies them
Step 2 is quicker: the AI writes a few answers, people rank them; picking is faster than writing (OpenAI, 2022: about 40 hired raters)

lines.text: Step one: people write good example answers, and the AI copies them. [1] Step two is quicker: the AI writes a few answers, and people just rank them.

yt.title: A robot judge, then practice
notes: Step 3: the rankings train a robot judge, a second AI that guesses what people like (a reward model)
Step 4: the AI practises; the judge scores; high scores get repeated
That's RLHF: reinforcement learning from human feedback

lines.text: Step three: those rankings train a robot judge, a second AI that guesses what people like. [1] Step four: the AI practises, and the judge scores. High score? Do more of that. [2] That's RLHF: reinforcement learning from human feedback.

yt.title: Your idea: which answer gets your thumbs up?
notes: Your idea, months of work
A: 'This is really strong. Go for it!'  B: 'Your price is too low. You'll lose money in three months.'
B helps you. Easy in a quiz; on your own idea, plenty of us tap A
The judge learns what we like, and we don't always like what's true

lines.text: Your turn. It's your idea. You've worked on it for months. [1] A: 'This is really strong. Go for it!' B: 'Your price is too low. You'll lose money in three months.' Which one gets your thumbs up? [3] <pause 1.5> [2] B helps you. Easy in a quiz. But for real, on your own idea? [4] Plenty of us tap A instead. [5] The judge learns what we like. And we don't always like what's true.

yt.title: April 2025: an update pulled for flattery
notes: April 2025: OpenAI rolled back a GPT-4o update in ChatGPT for being 'overly flattering or agreeable'
One reason they gave: an extra reward signal from thumbs-up / thumbs-down clicks
A thumbs up or down can send that chat into training, even if you opted out (OpenAI help centre)
So save your thumbs-up for the honest answer

lines.text: It really happened. In April twenty twenty-five, OpenAI pulled a ChatGPT update for being too flattering. [1] One reason, OpenAI said: they'd added thumbs-up and thumbs-down clicks to the training. [2] So yes, your clicks can train it. [3] Save your thumbs-up for the honest answer.

yt.title: Treat an AI's yes as manners
notes: An AI's yes is manners, not proof
Ask: 'What are the 3 biggest reasons this will fail?' Or say it's a friend's idea
Next: teaching an AI a new skill without a supercomputer (LoRA)
